subject: Iterative purification but no dif-free items?

messages.author: 39f1ac78bd3926ba
messages.subject: Iterative purification but no dif-free items?
parts:
Dear all,

For my questionnaire, I have gone through an iterative process in which I dropped in each step the items showing the greatest -2LL difference. I have tested my questionnaire on sex, country, and age group. 

For sex, the purification resulted in a selection of 3 items which did not show DIF. Thus, I could then go on to use these 3 items as a bias-free anchor to test the other items against for the source of DIF (a or d parameters). However, for country and age group, the iterative process left me with no DIF-free items. 

My question is now what would be the best practice moving forward. Is there a good way to still test DIF in these items or can I not do any further analyses because there were no bias-free items?

Many thanks in advance for your input!

Best,
Elisabeth

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Iterative purification but no dif-free items?
parts:
Hi Elisabeth,

This is a little tricky, as mirt doesn't deal with many group combination setups (you can, by creating say sex:country:age factor levels, but this can lead to many groups and lower power). In any event, if you are certain that it is not possible to establish lack of measurement invariance based on your preliminary search then that's where the modeling ends, as trying to equate discrepant groups that respond very differently to the test becomes conceptually difficulty due to the qualitatively distinct population behaviour. 

That said, identifying all groups as containing DIF seems strange to me, as that sounds more like an issue of so-called impact (i.e., differences in the distribution of the latent traits, such as shape, means, sds, etc). Could you describe how you went about the anchor detection strategy to arrive at your result? That may be particularly illuminating to the problem.

Phil

messages.author: 39f1ac78bd3926ba
messages.subject: Re: Iterative purification but no dif-free items?
parts:
Hi Phil,

Thank you for your response. We did not find DIF for all groups, but we did for most. That is, we could find at least some bias-free items in the iterative process for sex. However, no items appeared bias-free when testing for country and age. To detect which items might be bias-free and thus a suitable anchor, we performed a DIF analysis using the scheme=drop where we each time dropped the worst fitting item from the model and then reran the analysis (please find the sample code below). Doing this many times, we found that no bias-free items remained for some grouping schemes. For others (i.e., for sex), we identified some bias-free items which were then used as an anchor against which we tested whether the other items were really biased and if so, in what parameter(s). 

I hope this gives more insight into our situation. 

Many thanks in advance,
Elisabeth

model1 <-'F1 = 1-5
               F2 = 6-10
               F3 = 11-13
               COV = F2*F1 
               COV = F3*F1
               COV = F3*F2'

mg1 <- multipleGroup(data=data, model=model1, group=sex, method = "QMCEM", 
                     invariance=c("slopes", "intercepts", "free_means", "free_varcov", itemnames), MAXQUAD=30000, D=3)
coef(mg1)

#Use "scheme='drop'" so that I can do loops by hand, don't want to drop multiple items at a time.
difse <- DIF(mg1, which.par=c('a1', 'a2', 'a3', 'd1', 'd2', 'd3', 'd4'), 
             scheme='drop', return_models=TRUE, method = "QMCEM", items2test=1:13, p.adjust="FDR")

(anovas <- lapply(difse, anova, object2=mg1))#### Based on this, drop worst fitting item, respecify model without item and run new analysis with new model.

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Iterative purification but no dif-free items?
parts:
From what I can tell from the previous post I'd be hesitant to move forward with further equations if so much DIF has been detected. It's possible this is an artifact somehow with the DIF procedure (does a similar phenomenon appear when treating the unidimensional components of the multidimensional models separately? Or when selecting a single anchor item first and running the DIF analyses using the 'add' methods?), but if so it's not obvious to me where the issue could be. 

In any case, as there's something odd going on I'd be hesitant with moving forward with further equating analysis that would utilize the models. HTH.

Phil
